llm.summary: This Amazon Orders skill is coherent, but it handles sensitive buyer/order data and can change shipment-related order state while saving full responses locally by default.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the scripts: Amazon SP-API order search, order detail, buyer/address access, shipment updates, verification updates, and shipment confirmation. Those capabilities are high-impact because they expose customer/order data and can mutate Amazon order state.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill documents live POST/PATCH operations but does not require an explicit confirmation or dry-run before shipment or verification changes, and it does not scope when sensitive buyer/address endpoints should be used.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No auto-install or persistence hook was found. The dependency checker searches common local skill locations for linkfox-amazon-store-auth and exits if it is missing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Network use and API-key access are purpose-aligned and disclosed, but requests relay LinkFox API credentials, Amazon access tokens, request paths, queries, and bodies through a LinkFox gateway; users must trust that gateway with order operations.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill intentionally writes complete API responses to local JSON files and may print full small responses to stdout. Code can fall back to home or temp linkfox directories even though SKILL.md says /tmp is forbidden and the current directory should fail if unwritable.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use only in a trusted workspace with a legitimate Amazon seller operations need, restrict the LinkFox API key and Amazon permissions, avoid --inline for PII-bearing endpoints, delete saved linkfox response files when no longer needed, and require a clear human confirmation before running shipment or verification update scripts.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Environment variables, scripts, file writes, and network calls are expected for this integration, but the artifact does not declare tight permission boundaries for sensitive order handling.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Full raw response persistence is implemented and disclosed, but it is not proportionate by default for buyer, address, and regulated order data without redaction or retention controls.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The persistent session artifact store is broader than necessary and can use multiple local locations, including home or temp fallback paths.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The always-save behavior is artifact-backed and materially concerning because complete Amazon order responses may include customer PII.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The code writes complete results before any user-facing save confirmation; the later save message is not enough control for sensitive commerce data.
[SQP-2] expected: Use of /spApi/developerProxy is clearly part of the skill design and documented, but it expands the trust boundary to the LinkFox gateway.
[SQP-2] expected: confirmShipment is a stated feature, but the script performs the live POST without an artifact-level confirmation or dry-run guard.
[SQP-2] expected: getOrderAddress is a stated feature, but it returns and persists shipping-address data without minimization or access gating.
[SQP-2] expected: getOrderItemsBuyerInfo is a stated feature, but it returns and persists buyer information without minimization or access gating.
[SSD-3] unexpected: Printing and storing full sensitive order responses by default creates avoidable exposure in terminals, logs, synced folders, and shared workspaces.
